BiblicalUsage: Baalis was the king of the Ammonites who sent Ishmael to kill Gedaliah, the governor Nebuchadnezzar had left over the remnant in Judah, and Johanan warned Gedaliah, but Gedaliah would not believe him — and Ishmael came and slew him at Mizpah. One king, one plot, and the ruin of the remnant.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Gedaliah's refusal to believe the warning is one of the saddest moments in Jeremiah, and Baalis is the name behind it — a foreign king who finished what Babylon started.
